violations.category: Exposed secrets and unsafe deployment permissions
violations.description: AWS credentials hardcoded as environment variables in the Dockerfile.
violations.recommendation: Remove hardcoded credentials from the Dockerfile and use IAM roles for tasks or secure secret management services (e.g., AWS Secrets Manager, Parameter Store).

violations.description: S3 bucket configured with PublicRead access control.
violations.recommendation: Change the bucket AccessControl to Private and use bucket policies or Origin Access Control (OAC) if public access is required for a CloudFront distribution.

violations.description: S3 bucket configured with public-read ACL.
violations.recommendation: Set the ACL to 'private' and manage permissions via IAM policies or Bucket Policies instead.

violations.category: Exposed secrets and unsafe deployment permissions
violations.description: IAM role policy grants administrative access by using wildcards for both Action and Resource.
violations.recommendation: Restrict the IAM policy to follow the principle of least privilege by specifying only the required actions and resources.

violations.category: Exposed secrets and unsafe deployment permissions
violations.description: IAM policy grants administrative access by using wildcards for both Action and Resource.
violations.recommendation: Specify explicit actions and resources to adhere to the principle of least privilege.

violations.description: Security group rule allows unrestricted SSH access (port 22) from the public internet.
violations.recommendation: Restrict the CIDR range to a specific trusted IP range or use AWS Systems Manager Session Manager instead of SSH.

violations.description: Security group rule allows all protocols and all ports from the public internet.
violations.recommendation: Change the security group ingress rule to permit only the specific ports and protocols required by the application and restrict the CIDR range.
